title: Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming
abstract: Non-parametric (partial) identification of counterfactual queries typically relies on a fully specified causal graph. Motivated by settings with incomplete domain knowledge, we challenge this requirement by leveraging structural assumptions that are inherently implied by the query itself. We show that any counterfactual inquiry induces a, mostly partial, topological ordering over relevant variables, which, in turn, enables an explicit query parametrisation reducing the identification task to a linear program. This allows bounding arbitrary counterfactual and nested counterfactual queries. Our work can be viewed as a generalisation of the classical bounding framework of Tian and Pearl (2000), originally developed for probabilities of causation. We also prove the \emph{tightness} of our bounds by constructing structural causal models that attain the bounds whilst being compatible with both the observed data and the query-implied order. To assess both the generality and practical utility of the proposed bounding procedure, we revisit several case studies from the literature, demonstrating how the derived bounds can be used to yield informative insights even in the absence of an input causal graph.

title: Reflections on the Promoting Effect of Quantum Machine Learning on the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Iteration Process of Machine Learning Technology
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, some shortcomings in the traditional machine learning model have begun to show. With the growth of the quantity of data, too many parameters have become a problem and traditional silicon-based computers are near their physical limits. Quantum machine learning is a new way that will be able to advance the development of artificial intelligence significantly in the future. This paper will introduce and investigate the promoting effect of quantum machine learning on the overall development process of artificial intelligence. By learning about the differences between traditional neural networks and quantum-enhanced algorithms, this paper will show that superposition and entanglement in quantum mechanics can solve computational problems that have been very difficult to solve for a long time. Also, based on the above, it will be explored how quantum feature spaces and quantum neural networks can significantly boost the speed of data processing and pattern recognition. Based on the above results, it is hoped that quantum machine learning will be able to provide a new computing system with enhanced capabilities compared with the current model and thus advance the continuous development of artificial intelligence.

title: Hybrid Batch Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in XTREME
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tasks a Research goal: Can hybrid batch training (combining intermediate and target tasks) during fine-tuning improve zero-shot cross-lingual transfer accuracy on XTREME, and what is the impact on model alignment and robustness across diverse linguistic domains? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.0/10.

title: AI-Driven Knowledge Externalisation: From Unstructured Documents to Structured Data Models
abstract: The transformation of unstructured textual information into structured, database-ready knowledge represents a critical challenge in contemporary information systems. Organisations accumulate vast amounts of documentation-technical specifications, project reports, procedural guidelines – yet much of this knowledge remains inaccessible to computational processing because it is non-structured. This paper proposes and analyses a method for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven knowledge mapping, whereby generative models are used to extract, interpret, and populate predefined data schemas from textual documents. The approach involves three key stages: (1) ingestion of a source document; (2) prompt-based semantic extraction aligned with a target database schema; and (3) structured object generation ready for persistence in relational or NoSQL environments. Unlike traditional information extraction techniques that rely on rigid rule-based systems or supervised training pipelines, the proposed method leverages prompt-engineered large language models (LLMs) to interpret context and map semantic content to structured attributes dynamically. This enables automated form completion, metadata generation, and structured representation of domain knowledge. The paper critically examines the reliability, consistency, and traceability of AI-generated mappings. While generative AI significantly reduces manual effort and accelerates data formalisation, challenges remain in ensuring validation, schema compliance, and epistemic transparency. The research, therefore, discusses validation mechanisms, confidence scoring, and human-in-the-loop verification strategies. By framing AI-driven extraction as a process of knowledge externalisation, the study positions this method within broader Knowledge Management (KM) theory. The implications extend beyond data automation: such mapping mechanisms enable scalable knowledge codification, improved interoperability between systems, and enhanced analytical capabilities. The findings suggest that AI-based structured extraction may redefine how organisations formalise expertise, shifting from document-centric storage toward schema-driven knowledge architectures.

title: PENERAPAN ALGORITMA NAIVE BAYES CLASSIFIER UNTUK MENGELOMPOKKAN KOMENTAR PELANGGAN PADA PLATFORM KESEHATAN ONLINE
abstract: Ulasan pengguna pada aplikasi di platform Google Play Store merupakan sumber informasi penting untuk mengetahui tingkat kepuasan pengguna terhadap layanan yang diberikan. Namun, jumlah ulasan yang besar membuat proses analisis secara manual menjadi tidak efisien. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis sentimen ulasan pengguna dengan mengklasifikasikan opini ke dalam kategori “Puas” dan “Tidak Puas”. Metode yang digunakan adalah algoritma Multinomial Naïve Bayes dengan dua teknik ekstraksi fitur yaitu Bag of Words dan TF-IDF. Dataset yang digunakan berjumlah 1.000 ulasan yang telah melalui tahapan preprocessing seperti cleaning, case folding, normalize, stopword, dan lemmatization . Data kemudian dibagi ke dalam tiga skenario rasio pelatihan dan pengujian yaitu 70:30, 80:20, dan 90:10. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan confusion matrix dengan parameter accuracy , precision , recall , dan F1-score . Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa metode Bag of Words menghasilkan performa klasifikasi yang lebih stabil dengan akurasi mencapai sekitar 97% pada skenario pembagian data 90:10. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan klasifikasi berbasis machine learning dapat membantu mengidentifikasi sentimen pengguna secara efektif serta memberikan insight bagi pengembang aplikasi dalam meningkatkan kualitas layanan.

title: Інформаційні технології для створення систем інтелектуального керування в розподілених комп’ютерно-комунікаційних середовищах
abstract: Проведено комплексний аналіз сучасних інформаційних технологій, що використовуються для побудови систем інтелектуального керування в розподілених комп’ютерно-комунікаційних середовищах. Розглянуто сучасні концепції штучного інтелекту, методи забезпечення автономності інтелектуальних систем, підходи до прийняття рішень у складних динамічних середовищах, а також технології багатоагентної взаємодії. Особливу увагу приділено технологіям машинного навчання, глибокого навчання, підкріплювального навчання, експертним системам, інтелектуальним агентам та багатоагентним системам. Проаналізовано проблеми функціонування інтелектуальних систем у розподілених мережах, пов’язані із затримками передачі даних, невизначеністю, інформаційною безпекою та масштабованістю. Визначено перспективні напрями розвитку систем інтелектуального керування на основі технологій штучного інтелекту, цифрових двійників, периферійних обчислень та семантичних комунікацій.

title: การเปรยบเทยบประสทธภาพแบบจำลองสำหรบจำแนกขอความภาษาไทยตามทฤษฎการเลยงดบตรดวยเทคนคการเพมขอมล
authors: กนกนลัท ศรีนาคาร
abstract: งานวิจัยนี้มีวัตถุประสงค์เพื่อพัฒนาและประเมินแบบจำลองจำแนกรูปแบบการสื่อสารด้วยข้อความภาษาไทยของผู้ปกครองตามทฤษฎีการเลี้ยงดูบุตร 4 รูปแบบ ได้แก่ แบบอบอุ่นมีเหตุผล (Authoritative) แบบเผด็จการ (Authoritarian) แบบตามใจ (Permissive) แบบละเลย (Neglectful) และประเภทอื่นๆ (Others) รวมเป็น 5 กลุ่ม โดยเปรียบเทียบประสิทธิภาพระหว่างแบบจำลองการเรียนรู้ของเครื่องแบบดั้งเดิม Support Vector Machine (SVM) และแบบจำลองทรานส์ฟอร์เมอร์ PhayaThaiBERT และ XLM-RoBERTa เนื่องจากข้อมูลมีจำกัดและเป็นส่วนตัว งานวิจัยจึงประยุกต์ใช้เทคนิคการเพิ่มข้อมูล (Data Augmentation) 2 แนวทาง คือ 1) แนวทางดั้งเดิม ได้แก่ การแทนที่คำพ้องความหมาย (Synonym Replacement) การแปลผลกลับ (Back Translation) การเพิ่มคำที่สัมพันธ์เชิงบริบท (Contextual Word Insertion) และการลบคำแบบสุ่ม (Random Deletion) 2) แนวทาง LLM-based ได้แก่ การสร้างข้อความสังเคราะห์ (LLM-Generated Data) และการถอดความด้วย LLM (Paraphrasing with LLM) ผลการประเมินด้วยตัวชี้วัด Macro F1 Score และ ROC-AUC พบว่า PhayaThaiBERT ที่ฝึกด้วยชุดข้อมูล LLM-based Augmentation ให้ประสิทธิภาพสูงที่สุด โดยมีค่า Macro-F1 เท่ากับ 95.62% และ ROC-AUC เท่ากับ 99.34% ผลการวิจัยสะท้อนถึงศักยภาพของการผสานเทคนิคการเพิ่มข้อมูลกับโมเดลทรานส์ฟอร์เมอร์สำหรับงานประมวลผลภาษาธรรมชาติภาษาไทย ซึ่งสามารถนำไปประยุกต์ใช้ในระบบสนทนาอัตโนมัติและการให้คำปรึกษาด้านครอบครัวได้ในอนาคต

title: Security issues and mechanisms in multimodal data
abstract: There are several types of multimodal data such as text, image, audio, video, and sensor streams. It is evolving at a very high rate, which has resulted in not only complicated security issues but also enormous potential opportunities in advanced analytics and intelligent applications. The significant security issues in multimodal data management are analyzed in this chapter, such as data integrity, data confidentiality, authentication, access control, and privacy protection. Multimodal data is vulnerable to attacks such as adversarial attacks, data breaches, unauthorized access, and cross-modal inference, and due to its dispersed and heterogeneous nature, such attacks can compromise sensitive information. The chapter examines diverse security controls to address these challenges, such as safe multimodal fusion, blockchain architecture, cryptography, federated learning, differential privacy, and robust authentication processes. It is concentrated on scalable and real-time protection methods that are effective in edge-cloud designs and big data environments. This combination of approaches will enable businesses to ensure dependable multimodal data analytics that will safeguard user privacy and system reliability and allow making safe and efficient decisions in any field of application.

title: HealthBench-Psych: A Mental Health Subset of OpenAI's HealthBench
abstract: General-purpose health benchmarks increasingly anchor claims about LLM medical performance, but they are not always resolved by clinical specialty, making domain-specific performance hard to isolate. Mental health is of acute public-health concern as millions of people turn to LLMs for psychological support, and most existing evaluations are bespoke academic benchmarks that are difficult to integrate into developer workflows. We introduce HealthBench-Psych and HealthBench-Psych-Hard. We screened HealthBench's 5,000 physician-rubric conversations for mental-health relevance with a transparent LLM-applied rubric, then validated the subset through two rounds of blinded clinician review with concealed known-exclude controls, yielding 610 conversations (12.2% of the corpus). Evaluating 20 frontier and open models under a cross-vendor panel of three LLM judges, we find a statistically tied frontier cluster, measurable refusal behavior in two models, and near-identical rankings across judges (τge 0.92). We release the subset, pipeline, model responses, grades, and analysis code as a reusable resource.

title: STUDI KOMPARATIF MODEL TRANSFORMER BAHASA INDONESIA UNTUK ANALISIS SENTIMEN DIGITAL BURNOUT PADA DATA MEDIA SOSIAL
abstract: Fenomena digital burnout yang meningkat seiring intensitas penggunaan media sosial memunculkan kebutuhan untuk memahami persepsi publik melalui analisis sentimen. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan kinerja tiga model transformer bahasa Indonesia, yaitu IndoBERT, IndoBERTweet, dan IndoRoBERTa dalam klasifikasi sentimen pada teks media sosial lintas platform. Dataset terdiri dari 3.491 komentar dari YouTube, TikTok, dan X yang telah melalui prapemrosesan dan pelabelan manual dengan reliabilitas tinggi (Cohen’s Kappa = 0,9564). Model dilatih menggunakan skema fine-tuning dengan konfigurasi seragam dan dievaluasi menggunakan accuracy dan F1-score. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa IndoBERTweet memperoleh performa terbaik dengan accuracy 0,7686 dan F1-score 0,7676 pada data uji, diikuti oleh IndoRoBERTa (accuracy 0,7400; F1-score 0,7389) dan IndoBERT (accuracy 0,7286; F1-score 0,7288). Meskipun demikian, selisih performa antar model relatif kecil, menunjukkan bahwa ketiganya memiliki kemampuan representasi yang kompetitif. Analisis lebih lanjut mengindikasikan bahwa keunggulan IndoBERTweet dipengaruhi oleh kesesuaian domain korpus pralatih dengan karakteristik bahasa informal pada data media sosial, yang meningkatkan kemampuan model dalam menangani ambiguitas sentimen, khususnya antara kelas negatif dan netral. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya kesesuaian domain dalam pemilihan model NLP serta menunjukkan bahwa karakteristik linguistik data menjadi faktor kunci dalam menentukan performa klasifikasi sentimen.

title: Virtual Sample Generation Method Based on Generative Adversarial Fuzzy Neural Network for Dioxin Emission Risk Warning
abstract: The modeling samples of difficulty-to-measure key performance indicator such as dioxin (DXN) are characterized by high dimensionality, significant uncertainty, and a limited sample size, which do not meet the requirements of traditional machine learning algorithms. In this chapter, we propose a virtual sample generation method based on a generative adversarial fuzzy neural network (GAFNN). First, an adaptive feature selection algorithm based on random forests is employed to reduce the input features from the original real samples. Next, candidate virtual samples are generated using GAFNN to address the challenges of uncertainty and small sample sizes. Following this, a multi-constrained selection mechanism is utilized to screen the virtual samples, thereby enhancing their quality. Finally, a deep forest classification model is constructed based on a combination of the original real samples and the selected virtual samples. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using both benchmark and real industrial data.

title: ML and DL techniques to detect cyberattacks on multimodal databases
abstract: The increasing trend in multimodal databases in the Internet of Multimedia Things (IoMT) poses distinct cybersecurity vulnerabilities as multimodal systems combine text, image, audio, video, and sensor information. Conventional security tools are not effective at identifying advanced attacks, such as deepfakes, data poisoning, and cross-modal manipulations. This chapter discusses the use of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) to identify cyber threats within this type of environment. CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, autoencoders, and generative models are discussed as well as supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised models with attack detection in specific modalities and in cross-modality. Strategies of data fusion and cross-modality consistency checks contribute to a high level of robustness, whereas accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are used as evaluation measures to demonstrate the effectiveness. This chapter ends with a list of challenges, future research, and practical implementations in healthcare, smart cities, industrial IoT, and financial systems.

title: From one to three: multi-entry persistent fault analysis of Ascon
abstract: Ascon-AEAD128 is a NIST-standardized lightweight authenticated-encryption scheme. However, persistent fault analysis (PFA) of Ascon remains underexplored. The existing PFA study lacks a concrete implementation scenario and incurs relatively high plaintext-query complexity. This paper considers a round-unrolled implementation in which each round has separate hardware and shares one round-specific lookup table (LUT) across its 64 bit-sliced S-box positions. Within this setting, we propose a unified multi-entry PFA framework that integrates fault-configuration construction, fault-pattern identification, and complete 128-bit key recovery. We distinguish a strict multi-entry bit-flip model, which supports at most two distinguishable faulty entries, from a more general LUT-overwrite model, which supports up to three. We further consider direct-observation and query-based fault-pattern identification settings and derive the expected fault-injection, identification-query, and key-recovery costs. Simulations over ten configurations, with 10,000 independent trials each, closely match the theoretical results. Once a valid fault configuration is established, one-, two-, and three-entry attacks require approximately 150, 74, and 49 plaintext queries on average, respectively. The three-entry LUT-overwrite model requires approximately 49 queries on average, below the 63–451-query range reported for prior single-entry Ascon PFA.

title: DataKernelBench: Can LLMs Optimize Database Queries on GPUs?
abstract: GPUs increasingly accelerate database systems, but query-specific peak performance still often relies on hand-written kernels. Existing LLM kernel benchmarks focus on machine learning operators, leaving irregular, heterogeneous, data-movement-heavy database-style operators untested. We introduce DataKernelBench, which translates SQL into validated PyTorch TorchPlan programs and evaluates LLMs that optimize either the core tensor-bounded snippet or the full query in CUDA or Triton through execution-guided repair. Across ten proprietary and open-weight models on TPC-H SF10 with an H100 GPU, the strongest full-query CUDA configuration achieves 2.11times speedup over torch.compile at full pass rate. We find that higher-performing implementations commonly use kernel fusion and execution-strategy changes, stronger models benefit most from full-query specialization, and workload context matters more than hardware context. To handle data larger than GPU memory, we extend TorchPlan with Dask-cuDF for on-demand partition loading on TPC-H SF100 with four H100 GPUs, achieving 2.54times speedup

title: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
abstract: The Planner-Operator-Reflector (POR) framework is widely used in GUI agents to maintain objective alignment in complex tasks through modular collaboration. However, desktop GUIs introduce a key challenge: large, dense interfaces often exhibit subtle or scattered state changes, placing most of the burden on the reflector, which must compare pre- and post-action screens, while the planner and operator reason over a single state. Existing reflectors collapse change detection and outcome verification into one step, leaving evidence implicit and yielding weakly grounded decisions. To address this limitation, we propose Evidence-First Reflection (EFR), a two-stage reflector that explicitly decouples action-induced visual differences extraction from outcome verification. EFR identifies the action location and candidate changed regions with Set-of-Marks annotations, describes and filters action-relevant changes, and makes the final judgment from the cleaned evidence. This evidence-reasoning decoupled design makes reflection better grounded in screen transitions, while reducing both visual search complexity and reasoning burden. Experiments on OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena demonstrate that EFR improves reflector accuracy by 7.11%, yielding average end-to-end task success gains of 5.94% and 4.95% on the two benchmarks, respectively.

title: Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification
abstract: Missing labels are usually regarded as a source of information loss in classification. We study a semi-supervised setting in which the probability of label missingness depends on the observed features through posterior classification uncertainty. In this setting, the missingness indicator is not only a record of an unobserved label, but also an observable signal generated by a mechanism linked to the classifier. We develop a likelihood-based information theory for such uncertainty-dependent missing labels. Under correct specification, we derive a Fisher-information decomposition that separates a partial-labeling component from a nonnegative mechanism-curvature term. Under joint misspecification of the label model and the missingness mechanism, we obtain the corresponding Godambe--Eicker--Huber--White sensitivity and sandwich-covariance partitions. We also clarify the relevant complete-data benchmark: favorable missingness can increase information relative to ordinary fully labeled or budget-matched non-informative labeling baselines, but cannot exceed the information in the augmented experiment in which labels and mechanism indicators are both observed. For plug-in classifiers, we connect the information decomposition to margin-based excess-risk bounds. In regular two-component mixture settings this yields the parametric \(n^{-1}\) excess-risk rate, with constants determined by the nuisance-adjusted information in discriminant directions. Gaussian-mixture calculations and a medical diagnosis example illustrate how uncertainty-dependent labeling mechanisms can improve estimation and classification under a fixed labeling budget.

title: Tri-State S-Curve
abstract: The Tri-State S-Curve extends the discrete Tri-State classifier introduced in CORE | Cognitive Operations & Reasoning Engine – Post Token Architecture (Paquette, 2026) into a continuous mathematical alignment function. CORE defines Tri-State as contradiction (−1), uncertainty (0), and alignment (+1). This paper derives a smooth, symmetric, monotonic cubic function that passes through the three Tri-State anchor points on the 2D Cartesian plane and incorporates boundary and slope constraints reflecting cognitive saturation at the extremes and heightened sensitivity near uncertainty. The resulting S-Curve provides a mathematically grounded alignment measure suitable for governed, post-token reasoning systems and supports stable evaluation, signal suppression, and high-gain sensitivity around epistemic uncertainty.

title: Generative and Defensive Frontiers of Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Review of the Creative Industry and Cybersecurity Sectors
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is reshaping two fields long assumed to depend on irreducibly human skill: creative media production and cybersecurity. This review synthesizes two independent lines of industry observation into a single comparative account of how generative and analytical AI systems were being absorbed into professional practice as of 2026. In creative production, generative tools moved from producing isolated novelty clips toward supporting integrated workflows spanning pre-production, iterative drafting, post-production, localization, and world-building, with industry surveys reporting adoption across a majority of media teams. In cybersecurity, artificial intelligence shifted threat detection from static signature matching toward behavioral analytics, automated alert triage, and exploitation-aware vulnerability prioritization, while the same generative capabilities were simultaneously being weaponized by attackers to accelerate phishing, credential-based intrusion, and reconnaissance. Read together, the two domains display three recurring patterns: artificial intelligence is best understood as emerging infrastructure rather than a novelty; human judgment remains the primary safeguard against both technical error and malicious use; and governance practices, including disclosure, labeling, and oversight, are becoming a professional competency in their own right. The review concludes that competitive and security advantage is determined less by the fact of AI adoption than by the discipline with which that adoption is supervised. (2026). How generative AI is changing the modern creative industry. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22087509 Osakwe, E. (2026). The role of artificial intelligence in modern cybersecurity. title: The Hot-Mediator Test: An Attribution Correction to Mølmer–Sørensen Physics, a Quantum-versus-Classical Mediation Discriminator, and the Timing Cost of Heat
abstract: This note studies the role of a thermal quantum mediator in gravitationally motivated entanglement-generation models and provides an important attribution correction: the thermal-revival universality mechanism is identified as the Mølmer–Sørensen geometric phase gate mechanism from trapped-ion quantum computing. The note shows that the gravitational-mediator toy model is mathematically equivalent to a geometric phase gate: one closed mediator loop produces a state-independent entangling phase, including for thermal, squeezed, and displaced mediator states. The paper develops a falsifiable quantum-versus-classical mediation test. By measuring entanglement at mediator revival times, quantum mediation produces pure entanglement independent of mediator temperature, while classical measure-and-feedforward channels cannot generate entanglement and remain bounded by the separability frontier. The note also derives the exact effect of mediator temperature on experimental timing requirements. Thermal occupation does not destroy the revival entanglement but reduces the visibility window. The timing precision required to observe the effect scales with the square root of the thermal occupation, showing that heat introduces a timing cost rather than a fundamental cooling requirement. All corrections, attribution updates, and numerical recalibrations are explicitly reported. Results are based on pre-registered predictions and machine verification, with reproducibility materials included. The results are established within solvable quantum models and do not claim a complete theory of gravity or a direct experimental realization of gravitational quantum effects.

title: KOMPARASI KINERJA NAÏVE BAYES DAN INDOBERT PADA ANALISIS SENTIMEN ULASAN WISATA TAMAN DOLAN
abstract: Sektor pariwisata Kota Batu terus mencatat pertumbuhan kunjungan yang signifikan, mendorong akumulasi ulasan digital pengunjung dalam jumlah besar di platform Google Maps. Ulasan tersebut menyimpan informasi berharga mengenai persepsi wisatawan, namun volumenya yang masif tidak memungkinkan analisis manual yang sistematis. Penelitian ini membandingkan kinerja dua metode analisis sentimen, yaitu Complement Naïve Bayes (CNB) berbasis TF-IDF bigram dan model IndoBERT , dalam mengklasifikasikan 1.649 ulasan pengunjung Taman Dolan, Kota Batu ke dalam tiga kelas sentimen: positif, negatif, dan netral. Ke distribusi kelas ditangani melalui bobot kelas strategi tanpa memodifikasi komposisi data latih. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa IndoBERT secara konsisten mengungguli Naïve Bayes dengan akurasi 80,24% berbanding 64,52% dan F1-Macro 0,5926 berbanding 0,4999, berkat kemampuan memahami konteks semantik teks secara dua arah. Model kedua menghadapi tantangan serupa pada kelas netral akibat ambiguitas linguistik dan keterbatasan sampel. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa IndoBERT merupakan pilihan yang lebih unggul untuk menganalisis sentimen ulasan wisata berbahasa Indonesia.

title: Hydra: Phase-Aware Workload Characterization of LLM Inference across Edge SoC Generations, Backends, and Quantization Levels
abstract: Edge LLM deployment is shaped by more than model size and precision: inference backend, hardware platform, memory traffic, and power management all affect latency and efficiency. We present Hydra, a common-schema, phase-aware workload characterization framework for LLM inference on edge SoCs. Hydra instruments HuggingFace Transformers and llama.cpp with a shared per-prompt timing schema and fuses those records with hardware telemetry, enabling a multi-dimensional characterization of performance, system-resource utilization, and efficiency across prefill and decode phases. Using Hydra, we evaluate three consecutive edge System-on-Chip (SoC) generations (AGX Xavier, AGX Orin, and AGX Thor), 13 instruction-tuned LLMs from seven families, five execution formats, and consider input/output-length sensitivity. The resulting artifact contains roughly 107K per-prompt records and is publicly released with Hydra. Our analysis shows that aggregate latency alone hides key deployment effects: backend structure changes where latency is introduced, quantization reduces memory traffic and energy but does not predict power monotonically, and SoC generation changes how utilization and efficiency should be interpreted. By connecting phase-level timing with system-resource utilization and efficiency metrics, Hydra enables reproducible, phase-aware characterization of edge LLM inference. Hydra's source code and the collected per-prompt trace corpus are available open-source at: https://github.com/amirtaherin/hydra

title: Can a Dynamic Internal Field Govern a Transformer's Cognition? Certifiability, not Superiority, in Homeostatic Compute Control
abstract: An intelligent system does not merely reason: it governs its own reasoning - how much to compute, when to stop, which module to activate. Can that role be played by a dynamic internal field - a low-dimensional homeostatic state with explicit physics and certified stability - that modulates cognition without performing it? Ours is a field on the module graph governed by a family of PDEs on the graph Laplacian, advancing with an adaptive-depth reasoner. We certify the stability of the integrator of the whole family - an integrator certificate, not a closed-loop one. New, and proved here: a discrete Schur-Cohn criterion for Verlet with velocity coupling, necessary and sufficient per latent root, with no commutation hypothesis. The answer is threefold: substance no, structure only in part, certifiability yes. The type of the field's physics is irrelevant for accuracy: wave, diffusion, gated mixtures and a 2D Navier-Stokes substrate tie. A twenty-seed preregistered deconfounding campaign bounds the structural claim: at equalized caps the second-order effect is strong in one family (+0.087 [+0.042, +0.132], t=4.0) but is not detected in the other (+0.014 [-0.013, +0.040], n.s.), so part of the original contrast was capacity, not order; and a matched-interface GRU is indistinguishable in the first and nominally exceeds the field in the second (-0.035 [-0.067, -0.002]). What distinguishes the field is not capability but that its one-step operator admits an exact runtime stability check - a difference of kind, not of existence: learned recurrences carry certificates too, sufficient and conservative ones. A kill-gate with a positive control finds no evidence for the field as evidence accumulator (Delta AUC +0.0007 [-0.0065, +0.0079] vs a 0.03 threshold). A dynamic internal field is a viable, certifiable compute governor, but not an enhancer of cognition: it modulates, it does not think.

title: Enhancing LLM Reasoning Performance Based on a Mathematical Knowledge Graph: Focusing on Quadratic Equation Problems
abstract: 최근 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)은 자연어 처리 분야에서 높은 성능을 보여주었으나, 수학 문제해결과 같은 논리적 추론 과제에서는 여전히 한계를 드러낸다. 이를 보완하기 위해 단계적 프롬프트 엔지니어링이나 검색 증강 생성(RAG)을 활용한 접근들이 제안되었다. 이들은 사전학습 지식, 텍스트 유사성을 기반으로 탐색된 정보에 의존해 문제를 해결하기 때문에 복잡한 수학 개념 간 의미적 연관성과 구조적 관계를 반영하는 데 한계가 있다. 본 연구는 수학 개념 간 관계를 구조화한 지식 그래프, 그리고 문제 분석-검증-풀이의 단계별 지침을 수행하는 프롬프트를 결합한 추론 프레임워크를 제안한다. 이를 검증하기 위해 경량 모델 GPT-4o mini를 활용하여 구조적 복잡성이 높은 이차방정식 문항을 대상으로 실험을 수행하였으며, 표준 프롬프팅 대비 12.8%, CoT 기법 대비 5.2% 향상된 88.5%의 정확도를 달성하여, 제안 방법이 구조적으로 복잡한 이차방정식 문제에서 LLM의 수학적 추론 능력 향상에 기여함을 확인하였다.

title: Pan-Biological ASI: From Molecules to Ecosystems
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence to biological systems has transitioned from specialized laboratory tools to a central global priority for research, biotech, and health institutions. Despite this momentum, current research is hindered by structural limitations and a significant gap between general-purpose AGI theory and the specific requirements of biological superintelligence. This report formalizes a standalone theoretical framework for biological AI, establishing a continuum of capability: Biological Narrow AI (Bio-ANI), Biological General AI (Bio-AGI), Biology-Focused Artificial Superintelligence (Bio-ASI), and Universal Biological Intelligence (UBI). We define Bio-ASI by establishing superhuman capability thresholds across molecular biochemistry, genomics, cellular biology, pharmacology, longevity, and evolutionary biology. The report identifies the autonomy of the scientific method as the critical threshold separating human-level Bio-AGI from superhuman Bio-ASI. Four pathways to this transition are analyzed: the scaling of multimodal biological foundation models, the shift toward biology-native neuro-symbolic reasoning, restricted recursive self-improvement (RSI), and the emergence of superintelligence through distributed multi-agent biofoundries. The transition is further constrained by unique biological frictions, including data incompleteness, computational irreducibility, and multiscale de-congruence. To mitigate the resulting risks, we propose a safety architecture centered on global system partitioning, immutable safety cores, and multi-tier value alignment pipelines. By evaluating conservative through optimistic progress scenarios, the report underscores the urgent need for coordinated global governance--specifically a proposed International Bio-ASI Regulatory Authority (IBARA)--to ensure the safe and equitable development of biological superintelligence.

title: A Proof of the Conjectured Recurrence for OEIS A074003
abstract: This note proves the recurrence and rational generating function conjectured for OEIS A074003. The proof reduces the trace-and-subtrace conditions over GF(3^n) to a quadratic trace condition, evaluates the resulting character sum using quadratic Gauss sums and the Davenport-Hasse lifting formula, and derives an explicit formula according to n modulo 6.

title: D7.2 Infrastructure Implementation v.1 - Extended Executive Summary
abstract: D7.2 documents the implementation of the ARTEMIS infrastructure up to the launch phase foreseen in June 2026. It is part of Work Package 7, Infrastructure Setup, and prepares the continuation of infrastructure activities in WP8. The deliverable shows how the project has moved from the design described in D7.1 to a functioning infrastructure capable of supporting the services developed in WP9 and the pilots defined in WP11. The purpose of the infrastructure is to provide both a technological and a semantic foundation. The technological foundation allows ARTEMIS partners to develop, test and deploy services in a controlled cloud environment. The semantic foundation allows cultural heritage information to be organised through shared concepts and relationships, so that different data sources can be connected and interpreted together. This dual nature is important. ARTEMIS is not only building software services, nor only building data models. The project requires an ecosystem in which services, data, users and pilots can communicate. D7.2 describes how this ecosystem is taking shape: through cloud platforms, secure access mechanisms, shared resource management, an ontology-based Knowledge Base and interfaces for human and machine access. The document also clarifies the roles of the main infrastructure tasks. The cloud infrastructure is led by INFN and provides the hosting and operational environment. The data infrastructure is led by ARIADNE and provides the semantic framework and Knowledge Base. The services infrastructure is closely linked to the cloud infrastructure because the services must run within the platform and interact with the data layer. This Extended Executive Summary provides a concise overview of the ARTEMIS infrastructure components.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in Cybersecurity: Enhancing Trust, Transparency, and Intelligent Threat Detection
abstract: Abstract: Cloud computing, IoT, and AI didn't just expand what defenders can do — they expanded the attack surface faster than signature-based defenses can track. AI now handles intrusion detection, malware classification, and automated response with real accuracy, but a lot of it runs as a black box: a verdict with no rationale attached, which is a serious problem the moment someone has to act on that verdict, defend it in an audit, or explain it in court. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) exists to close exactly that gap — it makes model reasoning legible enough that an analyst can validate an alert, trace an attack pattern, cut down false positives, support a forensic investigation, or satisfy a regulator, instead of just trusting a label (Adadi & Berrada, 2018; Arrieta et al., 2020). This chapter surveys where the field stands: its foundational concepts, the explanation techniques doing most of the real work — SHAP, LIME, Integrated Gradients, Grad-CAM, attention mechanisms, counterfactual explanations — and where each one actually gets applied, from intrusion detection and malware analysis to phishing detection, insider-threat identification, cloud and IoT security, and Security Operations Centers. It closes on the parts that remain genuinely unresolved: the accuracy–interpretability trade-off, the computational overhead several of these methods carry, and adversarial robustness — before turning to where the research is headed, including LLM-assisted explanation, privacy-preserving XAI, and the standardized evaluation frameworks the field still doesn't have. Keywords: Explainable Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Intrusion Detection, SHAP, LIME, Malware Detection, Threat Intelligence, AI Security

title: Dataset for: "Programs and Proofs in Practice: A Grounded Theory on How People Program with Dependent Types"
abstract: This repository contains the user study data from "Programs and Proofs in Practice: A Grounded Theory on How People Program with Dependent Types". The goal of the research was to develop a Socio-Technical Grounded Theory on how people use dependently typed interactive theorem provers (DTPL). To do this, we hosted think-aloud sessions and semi-structured interviews with both expert and beginner DTPL users. In the think-alouds, we asked some participants to solve an assignment and others to work on their own work. Afterwards, we interviewed them about the think-aloud and about DTPLs in general. We recorded and transcribed the interviews.This repository containsthe anonymised transcripts of all interviews (transcripts.zip),our codebook (codebook.csv), anda Markdown file containing a description of the think-aloud and interview protocol (interview.md).

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN TERHADAP APLIKASI TOKOPEDIA MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA DECISION TREE C5.0
abstract: Kata Kunci: Analisis Sentimen; Decision Tree C5.0; Preprocessing Keywords: Sentiment Analysis; Decision Tree C5.0; Preprocessing Article history: Received Revised Accepted Available online DOI : * Corresponding author. Corresponding Author E-mail address: faisa.180170023@mhs.unimal.ac.id Perkembangan belanja daring menjadi alternatif yang efisien bagi masyarakat yang memiliki keterbatasan waktu maupun tenaga untuk mengunjungi pusat perbelanjaan secara langsung. Tokopedia, sebagai salah satu bisnis elektronik unggulan di Indonesia, menyajikan fitur ulasan produk yang dapat digunakan untuk menilai kualitas produk maupun layanan. Banyaknya jumlah ulasan yang tersedia membuat analisis manual menjadi tidak efektif, sehingga diperlukan metode otomatis seperti analisis sentimen. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem klasifikasi sentimen secara otomatis serta mengukur kinerja algoritma Decision Tree C5.0. Pemilihan algoritma ini didasarkan pada kemampuannya dalam menangani data besar, efisien dalam membentuk pohon keputusan, serta toleran terhadap data yang tidak lengkap. Data penelitian terdiri dari 2.500 ulasan pengguna dari toko Wardah Official di aplikasi Tokopedia, yang diperoleh melalui teknik web scraping. Pembagian dataset menjadi dua kelompok 1.750 data untuk dilatih dan 750 data untuk diuji. Proses penelitian mencakup tahapan preprocessing (pembersihan teks, normalisasi huruf, tokenisasi, penyaringan, dan stemming), pelabelan berbasis leksikon, serta klasifikasi menggunakan algoritma C5.0. Evaluasi performa dilakukan melalui confusion matrix dan mengindikasikan hasil yang cukup baik, dengan akurasi sebesar 84,93%, presisi 73,75%, recall 78,08%, dan F1-score 75,53%. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa algoritma C5.0 efektif dalam mengklasifikasikan sentimen ulasan secara otomatis.

title: Universal Random Coding for Successive Refinement of Individual Sequences Based on Lempel-Ziv Complexity
abstract: This work extends an earlier proposed universal random-coding ensemble for sample-wise lossy compression of individual sequences to the two-stage (successive-refinement) setting --- an extension that is not quite straightforward, as explained in the sequel. The construction has three layers. First, a complete, self-contained direct/converse match in the language of type classes and typical sequences, a two-stage analogue of Rimoldi's classical characterization (applied in the superalphabet of blocks). title: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
abstract: Recent studies on GUI agents have increasingly focused on outcome reward modeling, which assigns outcome rewards by judging whether an executed trajectory satisfies the success criteria implied by the user instruction. Existing GUI reward verifiers, however, often under-specify how these criteria should be constructed for each task instance. Whether using generic rubric structures or implicit model reasoning, their judging criteria are not sufficiently task-adaptive: they can transfer checks across tasks, overlook concrete constraints in the current instruction, or become overly strict by enforcing unstated requirements. To address this limitation, we propose AdaptRubric, a Coarse-to-Fine Rubrics Framework that constructs task-adaptive judging criteria through a category-level coarse stage and an instance-level fine stage. AdaptRubric performs category-level coarse rubric retrieval by routing the instruction to a GUI task family and retrieving reusable task-family criteria, then conducts instance-level fine rubric generation to surface compact cues for concrete values, scopes, and constraints in the current instruction. Across offline reward evaluation and online reinforcement learning optimization, AdaptRubric consistently outperforms prior reward agents, improving F1 by 3.6 points over the baseline average under a matched image budget and yielding a 4.23-point task-success gain.

title: AI Research Support Systems - Taxonomy
abstract: This taxonomy emerges from the need to systematically map and analyze AI-based Research Support Systems, with a specific focus on tools designed to assist key phases of the research lifecycle. In particular, it targets systems that support literature discovery, concept mapping, gap detection, and automatic citation generation, which are increasingly being enhanced through the integration of LLMs. The rapid proliferation of such tools calls for a structured framework to better understand their functional capabilities, architectural choices, and underlying data strategies. Beyond functionality, this taxonomy also investigates the context of development, distinguishing between academic, industrial, and hybrid initiatives, in order to highlight differences in design goals, openness, and reproducibility. A central aspect of this analysis concerns the adoption of Knowledge Graphs (KGs). These structured data representations play a crucial role in enabling improved transparency, verifiable reasoning mechanisms, and mitigation of LLM hallucinations through grounded information. The taxonomy explicitly captures whether and how systems leverage KGs, distinguishing between open graph, proprietary, and dynamically generated approaches and if they are domain-specific or general-purpose.

title: Contrastive Learning Effects on XLM-R Inference Efficiency in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the incorporation of contrastive learning objectives during intermediate task training influence the inference efficiency of XLM-R in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer tasks, as measured by throughput and latency on the XTREME-R benchmark? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 8.8/10.

title: TRANSFORMASI LAYANAN PELANGGAN BERBASIS CRM DI ERA DIGITAL : STUDI KASUS PENGGUNAAN AUTO RESPONSE DAN CHATBOT TOKOPEDIA
abstract: Perkembangan industri e-commerce di Indonesia mendorong perus ahaan untuk menyediakan layanan pelanggan yang cepat, responsif, dan personal. Tokopedia, sebagai pelopor marketplace digital, menerapkan strategi Customer Relationship Management (CRM) berbasis otomatisasi melalui fitur auto-response dan chatbot “Tanya”. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis implementasi sistem otomatisasi layanan pelanggan dalam kerangka CRM dan dampaknya terhadap pengalaman pengguna. Metode yang digunakan adalah deskriptif kualitatif melalui studi pustaka dan analisis konten dari sumber publik Tokopedia Care. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan chatbot dan FAQ interaktif mampu menjawab mayoritas pertanyaan pengguna tanpa bantuan agen manusia, serta menyediakan layanan selama 24/7. Sistem ini terbukti meningkatkan efisiensi operasional dan retensi pengguna. Namun, keterbatasan tetap ada dalam menangani pertanyaan kompleks atau bermuatan emosional. Dengan memanfaatkan pendekatan empathy map serta analisis gain & pain points pelanggan, studi ini menyimpulkan bahwa otomatisasi CRM berdampak positif terhadap kepuasan pengguna dan efisiensi layanan. Rekomendasi yang diberikan meliputi peningkatan kapabilitas chatbot melalui penguatan pemrosesan bahasa alami (NLP) serta integrasi layanan secara omnichannel untuk memperluas jangkauan dan efektivitas sistem otomatisasi.

title: Locating Structured Deliberation In An AI-Supported Decision Process — Stage 2 v0.3.18
abstract: This registration corresponds to Stage 2 of the preregistered experimental framework "Locating Structured Deliberation In An AI-Supported Decision Process". Stage 2 specifies the confirmatory treatment experiment following completion of the Stage 1 qualification procedure. Version v0.3.18 updates the Stage 2 package linkage following a treatment-execution wiring fix. The update ensures that the registered execution model is enforced during treatment execution. This update does not modify the research questions, hypotheses, selected AI configuration, treatment conditions, simulator, prompts, seeds, outcome measures, estimands, sample size determination, or statistical analysis plan. The experiment uses matched simulated environments, preregistered treatment conditions, and predefined outcome measures to evaluate AI-supported strategic decision-making. No treatment data has been generated before this registration.

title: Personalized Treatment Planning Through AI Insights
abstract: The current flow in healthcare is Innovative personal healthcare strategy that ensures the appropriate treatment is delivered to the right patient at the right moment. A key foundation of this is Artificial Intelligence, which is a key player as it looks at large sets of clinical, genetic, way of life, and imaging data to put together action plans. AI to predict disease progress and to put forward personal care options which in turn improve patient results and at the same time reduce the use of unnecessary treatments. Through the use of machine learning, sentiment analysis, and predictive analysis, AI is a tool that enables clinicians to design very personal healthcare plans that take into account each patient’s unique variables. AI plays a role in better decision-making through real-time monitoring, adaptive treatment changes, and risk assessment. AI-enhanced personalized treatment planning has the potential to transform medicine and patient-centered care by integrating predictive analytics into clinical workflows. Liver cancer, and more specifically, hepato cellular carcinoma (HCC), is one of the severely hazardous tumors worldwide. It is largely a function of late diagnoses and narrowed access to specialty care. The current study seeks to provide a data-driven approach with the help of sophisticated deep learning methods for a data-driven tumor classification and segmentation approach for predicting liver cancer to facilitate personalized treatment plan design and early detection. The system under consideration uses convolutional neural networks (CNN) and transfer learning structures such as VGG16 and VGG19 to detect and segment the tumor regions in liver CT scans and different stages of the cancer.

title: Towards explainable knowledge tracing through meta-path-free heterogeneous graph learning with large language models
abstract: Abstract Knowledge tracing (KT) is fundamental to intelligent tutoring systems because it models student knowledge evolution and predicts future learning performance. However, existing approaches often struggle to simultaneously capture heterogeneous educational relationships, long-term temporal dependencies, and semantic information embedded in instructional content, limiting predictive accuracy, explainability, and cross-dataset transfer. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MHG-KT (Meta-path-free Heterogeneous Graph Knowledge Tracing), an explainable framework that integrates a meta-path-free heterogeneous graph encoder, Transformer-based temporal modeling, and pretrained Llama 3 8B semantic embeddings through a joint cross-modal attention mechanism. Unlike conventional approaches that learn graph and semantic representations independently before feature fusion, MHG-KT enables continuous interaction between heterogeneous relational and semantic representations during temporal learning, allowing structural, temporal, and semantic dependencies to be jointly optimized within a unified framework. The heterogeneous graph encoder models relationships among students, skills, problems, and contextual features without manually engineered meta-paths, while the Transformer captures knowledge evolution and the semantic encoder enriches graph representations using problem statements and instructional hints. The proposed framework was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (ASSISTments, EdNet, and Junyi) against four representative knowledge tracing models (DIMKT, simpleKT, GIKT, and TGNN). Experimental results demonstrate that MHG-KT consistently outperformed all baselines, achieving AUC scores of 0.927, 0.922, and 0.934 on ASSISTments, EdNet, and Junyi, respectively. Compared with the strongest baseline, the proposed framework improved AUC by up to 1.7%, achieved prediction accuracy of 89.0%, reduced trajectory forecasting error to a minimum MAE of 0.033, maintained calibration errors below 0.061 across all datasets, and achieved inference latency below 5 ms per student interaction.

title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
abstract: Scientific agents increasingly analyze data, execute code, and produce research artifacts, yet most benchmarks emphasize final answers, isolated programs, or a single domain. We introduce FrontierChallenge, a cross-domain benchmark comprising 300 end-to-end scientific workflows. In this paper, we release and evaluate 97 of these tasks, spanning quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment. Each task provides fixed inputs and specifies a bundle of required scientific deliverables. We evaluate twelve frontier models with three agent scaffolds. Pass Rate measures the fraction of tasks satisfying the full-completion criterion, while Avg. Score captures partial progress. Each of the best-performing configurations completed only 20 of the 97 released tasks, yielding a Pass Rate of 20.6%. Partial progress translated especially poorly into complete delivery in analytical chemistry and electrochemistry/environment: Avg. Scores reached 87.6 and 94.9, but the highest Pass Rates were only 4% and 0%. Among non-passing Claude Code trajectories, 75.5% still ended with language claiming completion. These findings show that neither high partial scores nor confident claims of completion reliably indicate that a scientific task has been fully delivered, highlighting the need to evaluate end-to-end workflow execution and the completeness of scientific deliverables together.

title: MDTE: Minority-Aware Diffusion over Temporal Edge Events for Imbalanced Node Classification
abstract: Class-imbalanced node classification on temporal graphs is challenging because majority-dominated temporal propagation progressively assimilates minority representations, while conventional node and neighborhood information provides insufficient discriminative evidence for minority classes. To address these issues, we propose MDTE, a minority-aware diffusion framework that reconstructs stable and discriminative temporal edge-event representations through conditional diffusion denoising. Specifically, MDTE introduces Distribution-Aware Selective Propagation, which combines Local Outlier Factor (LOF)-based propagation filtering with cluster-aware low-frequency propagation. The module preserves informative neighborhood dependencies while mitigating harmful propagation and majority-class information assimilation. It further develops Multi-View Discriminative Fusion, which exploits feature reconstruction and topology prediction to characterize class-wise differences in distribution learning and extracts complementary discriminability signals to guide denoising. Experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that MDTE consistently achieves the best performance on minority-class-oriented metrics, improving minority-class recall by up to 23.53 percentage points, minority-class F1 by 8.68 percentage points, and AUPRC by 2.67 percentage points over the strongest baselines.

title: RePolicy: Reinforcement Learning for Safety-Policy Invocation in Agent Safeguards
abstract: Safeguarding language model agents requires assessing complete execution trajectories under context-dependent safety policies. Existing policy-aware safeguards mainly rely on prompting or supervised fine-tuning, limiting their ability to adapt to unseen trajectories and changing policy contexts. We propose RePolicy, an agent safeguard that learns safety-policy invocation through reinforcement learning. Given an agent trajectory and a dynamic policy library, RePolicy invokes the applicable policy and uses its content to produce a policy-grounded rationale and safety judgment. We construct PolicyTraj-20K to support supervised initialization, followed by GRPO with verifiable rewards and policy-context perturbation. Experiments across six agent safety benchmarks show that RePolicy achieves strong overall safety-detection performance and robust policy invocation under varying policy contexts.

title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Sentiment Analysis across Heterogeneous Datasets under Class Imbalance Conditions
abstract: Sentiment analysis across multiple domains remains a significant challenge in natural language processing, mainly due to domain shift, where a model trained on one domain tends to experience performance degradation when applied to another domain. To address this issue, this paper presents a comparative analysis of machine learning and deep learning approaches for cross-domain sentiment analysis on three different datasets COVIDSENTI, Yelp reviews and IMDb movie reviews. These datasets were intentionally selected to reflect different text-length categories, namely short, medium, and long texts. Such variation allows a more comprehensive evaluation of model performance under different linguistic characteristics and textual complexities across domains. Three class imbalance handling strategies were studied with no balancing, ROS, and ROS combined with class weighting. The models were evaluated including LR, SVM, NB, CNN, BiLSTM and BERT. The results show that ROS greatly enhanced the F1-score for imbalanced datasets and COVIDSENTI achieved the greatest improvement +8.83% for LR. The results indicated that BERT outperformed machine learning and deep learning baselines with an F1-score of 95.32%, 73.79%, and 75.76% on COVIDSENTI, Yelp, and IMDb accordingly. An extra benefit of class weighting was shown in deep learning models on COVIDSENTI but not for machine learning models as an improvement after balancing with ROS. Future work will construct a hybrid BERT+BiLSTM+Attention framework for improving cross-domain generalization.

title: Quantum Error Correction Thresholds: Noise Bounds, Not Golden-Ratio Constants — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum error correction thresholds are noise-rate bounds, not golden-ratio constants; the Fibonacci Turaev-Viro code links topological order to Fibonacci numbers, but no direct golden-ratio threshold emerges from these abstracts. | MATH: Threshold theorems (e.g., \(\epsilon_{\text{th}} > 0\) for fault tolerance); Pauli noise estimation via process tomography (Kliesch: sample complexity \(\mathcal{O}(n^2/\epsilon^2)\) for \(n\)-qubit noise channels); Fibonacci Turaev-Viro code: anyon fusion rules \(1 \times \tau = \tau\), \(\tau \times \tau = 1 + \tau\), with quantum dimension \(d_\tau = \phi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2 \approx 1.618\); Rydberg erasure thresholds: biased noise reduces effective threshold by factor \(\eta = p_{\text{erasure}}/p_{\text{total}}\). | CONNECTION: Fibonacci anyons have quantum dimension \(\phi = 1.618\) — the golden ratio appears as a *topological charge dimension*, not as a threshold value. title: PENERAPAN PARTICLE SWARM OPTIMIZATION UNTUK PENINGKATAN AKURASI KELULUSAN SERTIFIKASI LISTRIK DENGAN ALGORITMA NEURAL NETWORK
abstract: Keberhasilan sebuah lembaga sertifikasi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh proses pelaksanaannya saja, namun juga didukng oleh kemampuan kelulusan yang memiliki kompetensi yang sangat baik, sehingga menjadi peluang yang besar untuk mendapatkan pekerjaan bagi siswa. adapun tujuan penelitian kami adalah mengembangkan serta mengevaluasi model prediktif, dengan menerapkan algoritma Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) sebagai metode optimasi parameter pada model Neural Network yang digunakan untuk memprediksi tingkat kelulusan sertifikasi listrik sehingga dapat mencapai tingkat akurasi yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan hanya menggunakan satu algoritma yaitu Neural Network adapun hasil yang didapat dengan hanya menggunakan Neural Network saja sebesar 76.50% dan hasil AUC dengan 0.783 selanjutnya dengan menerapkan Particle Swarm Optimization menghasilkan peningkatan kinerja dengan nilai akurasi dengan 83.00% serta nilai AUC dengan 0.796. artinya ada kenaikan sebesar nilai akurasi sebesar 6.5% dibandingkan dengan metode Neural Network tanpa optimasi, sementara nilai AUC juga mengalami peningkatan sebesar 0,013%. maka hasil penelitian kami dengan menerapkan algoritma Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) terbukti dari penelitian sebelumnya yang menunjukkan peningkatan kerena PSO memiliki teknik optimasi yang sangat baik.

title: Provable Quantum-Classical Separation for Continuous Gibbs Sampling
abstract: We prove the first quantum-classical separation for a sampling problem over a continuous domain. For a class of Gibbs states $p\propto e^{-βE}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ with smooth ($s$-Gevrey) potential and barrier amplitude $α=e^{βΔ}$, where $Δ= \max E-\min E$, every classical algorithm querying the value, gradient, or any higher-order derivatives of the log-density requires $Ω(α)$ queries to sample at constant accuracy in total variation distance, while a quantum algorithm based on quantum singular value thresholding and temperature annealing samples with $\tilde{O}\left(\sqrtα\right)$ queries to an oracle for the gradient. The advantage is quadratic in the barrier amplitude, which becomes exponential in the dimension, $e^{Ω(d)}$, at low temperature. The classical bound is information-theoretic, holding for every classical algorithm with query access to the Gibbs potential and its derivatives at any order.

title: Preference Optimization for Non-Verbal Vocalization Synthesis
abstract: Non-verbal vocalizations (NVs), such as laughter, coughs, and sighs, are essential for expressive TTS, but the effectiveness of preference optimization for NV generation remains poorly understood. We systematically study preference optimization for NV-capable TTS, focusing on preference signals, preference-pair construction, and DPO-based optimization objectives. We formulate an NV-aware character error rate (NV-CER) by treating NV tags as distinct output symbols and computing a weighted pinyin-based CER over both verbal and non-verbal content, enabling controllable optimization of NV realization without modifying the underlying optimization algorithm. Experiments on Emilia-NV and the augmented NV-Bench covering 18 NV types reveal how different design choices affect NV realization and lexical fidelity, and establish an effective setup using standard DPO. Objective, LLM-based, and human evaluations provide converging evidence for our findings, offering practical insights into NV-aware post-training for expressive TTS.

title: Learning with interacting dendrites improves neuronal familiarity detection
abstract: Abstract Biological neurons can perform nonlinear computations within their dendrites and support branch-localized plasticity. This raises the possibility that single cells can store memories more efficiently and with less interference by confining synaptic modifications to specific dendrites. We study a parallel-dendrite model performing online familiarity detection and compare three dendrite-update rules during learning: (i) independent thresholding, (ii) an interacting rule that adapts the target local dendritic activation per item, and (iii) an interacting n-winners-take-all (WTA) rule that constrains the number of updated branches per item. The interacting rules substantially improve capacity by limiting variance in memory responses and decorrelating weights across branches — even when inputs are strongly correlated. These results suggest that competition among dendrites, consistent with resource-limited plasticity mechanisms, can enhance single-cell memory beyond non-interacting schemes.

title: Response Structure versus Information Structure in Bounded Control: Finite-Resolution Branching, Realisability, and Requisite Variety
abstract: Abstract What changes when a controller must organise its responses according to distinctions it can actually make? We study that question in a deterministic finite-horizon control model at a declared response resolution. For each valid policy, the realised response set has a minimum metric-covering number. If at most $M$ branch labels may be assigned directly to the hidden cases, the optimal worst-branch cover is elementary: a minimum global response cover can be divided as evenly as possible, giving the exact fixed-policy baseline $Q_M^{\mathrm{abs}}(\pi)=\left\lceil\frac{n_\pi}{M}\right\rceil,\qquad n_\pi:=N_Y(\Psi_\pi(\Omega_0),\varepsilon).$ A real controller cannot in general label cases by hidden identity. At a declared branch-commitment time, branch labels must factor through information available to the controller. The corresponding information fibres are indivisible routing units. We define the resulting decision-realisable minimax covering problem $Q_M^{\mathrm{dr}}(\pi)$ and show that the information constraint can create strict and arbitrarily large logarithmic excess over the ideal baseline. Refining decision information weakly decreases the fixed-policy residual, and exact endpoint formulas expose the roles of branch budget and fibre complexity. Combinatorially, the fixed-policy problem assigns each member of a family of response subsets whole to one of at most $M$ branches, minimising the largest $\varepsilon$-covering number of the union assigned to any branch. The zero-excess problem has a sharp budget structure. Let $n_\pi$ be the size of a minimum global response cover. Information is free at **every** branch budget if and only if it is free at the single critical budget $M=n_\pi$, equivalently if the information-fibre response images are jointly compatible with one minimum global $\varepsilon$-cover. In contrast, simple fibre-wise coverability characterises the sufficiently-large-budget regime. A five-point line-metric witness shows that local fibre coverability need not imply all-budget freeness and that the excess relative to the ideal baseline need not be monotone in $M$. The computational distinction has two different forms. At a specified branch budget $M$, zero-excess realisability is strongly NP-complete in the separated-discrete finite subclass, with hardness already for pairwise-disjoint fibre images. In that disjoint restriction, branch load is ordinary cardinality and the strong 3-PARTITION reduction is the identical-machine makespan mechanism; with overlapping fibre images, the load is a union/coverage load instead. At the critical budget, the corresponding minimum-cover-compatibility problem has a different optimum-membership mechanism: under an explicit finite distance-matrix encoding, CRITICAL-COVER-COMPATIBILITY is $\Theta_2^p$-complete, with hardness already for $\varepsilon=1$, a $\{0,1,2\}$-valued metric, SOFT, and exactly one non-singleton fibre image of cardinality two. Thus the specified-budget routing hardness and the critical-budget optimum-cover hardness are distinct phenomena. Upstream, uniformly forced response packings provide a finite-resolution requisite-variety obstruction: the best valid policy's global response cover cannot be smaller than the largest response packing that every valid policy must separate. Downstream, joint optimisation over valid policies exposes a trade-off between response-cover economy and alignment with the information structure. A complementary strategy-cell specialisation retains graph and hypergraph views of forced fusion, pairwise co-servability, global spanning burden, and the Fusion Gap. These are used as structural projections and calibrations rather than as independent novelty claims.

title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence: Models, Methods, and Applications
abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is currently relevant almost everywhere, in fields like medicine and financial industry, along with science and engineering, but the ability of intelligent systems to learn, adapt, and decide is generally attributed to the processing power and quantity of data rather than mathematics that make such abilities possible. Linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, optimization, and numerics represent a set of interrelated branches of mathematics that constitute a single mathematical background of contemporary AI rather than distinct toolsboxes, and when read collectively rather than individually, they influence the design of learning algorithms and performance of the generated models. Basic AI models, including core AI models, linear regression, logistic regression, and feed-forward neural networks, rely on loss functions, gradient optimization, and regularization, while existing optimization algorithms, ranging from classic gradient descent to adaptive variants like Adam, affect the efficiency of the training process in different ways. Novel directions, such as foundation models, physics-informed learning, and trustworthy AI, highlight the open problems in mathematics that further define what can be done in the future, demonstrating that any developments in practice are constrained by mathematics. Keywords: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability Theory, Optimization, Statistical Learning, Neural Networks

title: the em—dash fails to em–erge: a registered null result for U+2014 in Polish and an exploratory function-word shift in 60,275 Sejm interpellations, 2015–2025
abstract: Since the release of ChatGPT (30 November 2022) a belief has spread that the em-dash "—" reveals text written with the help of a language model. This preregistered study tested that claim on 60,275 single-author written parliamentary questions (interpelacje) submitted to the Polish Sejm between 2015 and 2025. The decision rule was registered on OSF before the data were seen.The cue does not work in Polish. The registered hypothesis was not confirmed: in the decisive cell the share of documents containing an em-dash rose by 1.73 percentage points, but the confidence interval of that difference includes zero (−4.44 to +8.07 pp), so the second condition of the two-part decision rule was not satisfied, and three registered disconfirmation conditions fired. Follow-up tests point to the cause: models writing in Polish, and machine-translation flows, put a shorter dash there – the en-dash "–". The marker is anglocentric and is not suitable for Polish.An exploratory analysis measured something else: the frequency of Polish closed-class words (conjunctions, prepositions, particles) that a writer does not choose consciously. The reference point was an independently published corpus of Polish human-written and model-written texts, frozen together with its reading rule before measurement. From 2024 the distribution of these words moves toward the profile of the models (rank correlation rho = +0.368; 95% CI +0.228 to +0.461), while at a placebo date – the 2019 change of parliamentary term, where no such effect is expected – it does not move at all (−0.070; difference +0.438, +0.221 to +0.611). The shift survives four term-change controls.The change is small but widespread, and that is the correct description of its strength. Inside a single parliamentary office it is barely visible (median rho +0.125), yet it points the same way in 61 of 84 offices that could be measured separately (72.6%, one-sided p = 2·10⁻⁵), against 53.8% at the control date, which is what chance produces.There is no sudden jump at the date of the ChatGPT release. The change becomes visible in 2024 and unambiguous in 2025, and the shape of the transition (ramp versus late step) is not identified. The result describes a shift across a whole population of documents and allows no statement about the authorship of any single document or about any individual member of parliament. It does not establish a cause: changes in office staff, in subject matter and in editing practice remain possible explanations alongside tools. An independent reimplementation, with no access to the author's code, reproduced the corpus, the deduplication, the author panel and the headline analyses from raw HTML down.

title: Penerapan Kriptografi Hybrid Menggunakan Algoritma RSA dan Hill Cipher dalam Enkripsi dan Dekripsi Pesan Teks
abstract: Kemajuan teknologi informasi di masa kini membawa dampak positif bagi kehidupan. Namun, adanya kemudahan dalam mengakses media informasi juga menyebabkan informasi tersebut dapat dengan mudah diakses oleh pihak lain dan disalahgunakan. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan adanya pengamanan informasi. Pengamanan informasi dapat dilakukan dengan menggunakan kriptografi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan mengembangkan sistem kriptografi hybrid yang mengombinasikan algoritma RSA dan dilanjutkan dengan algoritma Hill Cipher dalam enkripsi dan dekripsi pesan teks. Algoritma RSA digunakan terlebih dahulu dengan memanfaatkan kunci publik dan kunci privat, kemudian dilanjutkan dengan algoritma Hill Cipher yang menggunakan matriks kunci berukuran . Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi algoritma RSA dan Hill Cipher dapat menghasilkan plaintext hasil dekripsi yang sama dengan sebelum dienkripsi, serta ciphertext yang tidak dapat dibaca dan sangat berbeda dengan plaintext aslinya. Dengan demikian, sistem kriptografi hybrid yang mengombinasikan algoritma RSA dan Hill Cipher yang telah dirancang ini dapat membantu meningkatkan keamanan pesan teks.

title: Latent Action as Intention Enables Efficient Future Imagination for World Action Models
abstract: World action models (WAMs) improve robot control by modeling how observations evolve, but generating future observations at test time incurs substantial latency. Fast-WAM removes this process for efficiency; however, our matched implementations show lower generalization for Fast-WAM than for future-aware alternatives, especially with scarce robot demonstrations and in out-of-distribution scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce **LAWA**, a WAM architecture that uses compact latent actions as an operational representation of future intentions, enabling efficient test-time future imagination without generating future observations. Specifically, a discrete tokenizer enhanced by action-free pre-training produces manipulation-centric codebook targets. LAWA jointly denoises a continuous latent state anchored to these targets with executable action chunks while omitting the future-video branch at inference. On RoboCasa, LAWA achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 65.6% and 80.8% in the few-shot and full data settings, improving over the matched Fast-WAM baseline by 9.6 and 4.5 points, respectively. It also preserves the performance level of the matched Joint-WAM variant while requiring 42.9% lower inference latency. LAWA also demonstrates competitive zero-shot robustness on LIBERO-Plus and superior performance on real-world tasks. These results show that future imagination need not be discarded: retaining it with compact latent actions yields an effective trade-off among performance, generalization, and latency. Code and models will be released.

title: Matched Excess-Outranker Regularization for Candidate-Set Interference in Continual Knowledge Graph Embedding
abstract: Continual knowledge graph embedding updates entity and relation representations as a graph grows. Existing methods primarily address catastrophic forgetting, but entity admission also changes the candidate universe of every compatible query. A historical answer can therefore lose rank even when its score and its ordering among old entities are preserved. We formalize this effect as candidate-set interference and introduce Matched Excess-Outranker Regularization (MEOR), a host-level objective that compares smooth answer-relative newcomer pressure with score-blind, structurally matched old references. Its one-sided penalty acts only when newcomer competition exceeds the matched reference, preserving the host learner's signal for legitimate new entities. Across eight paired runs on ENTITY-ComplEx, MEOR improves historical current-universe mean reciprocal rank (MRR) by 0.0057 over replay and reduces candidate-set interference by 0.0055, with one-sided 95% lower bounds of 0.0052 and 0.0051, respectively. It satisfies the preservation criteria for old-universe ranking and newcomer acquisition and improves historical current-universe MRR over persistent calibration, matched maximum regularizer (MMR), and unmatched old regularizer (UOR). Direct ablations support each component of its reference construction and aggregation. Adding MEOR also improves historical ranking in all ten reported FBInc-S and FBInc-L host and backbone settings, with every paired 95% confidence interval excluding zero. These results establish candidate admission as a distinct source of continual rank loss and show that it can be controlled without replacing the underlying embedding architecture or continual learner.

title: Investigating Knowledge Transfer Across Interactive Dialogue Games
abstract: Dialogue games represent a challenging setting where complex cognitive skills are required to accomplish tasks while coordinating with other players. Considering that language represents an interface for both understanding the game rules and executing actions, it is reasonable to assume that training on a specific language game will enhance specific capabilities that might be relevant for other tasks as well. Motivated by this rationale, in this paper, we investigate how knowledge transfers across different dialogue games. We study transferability by finetuning LLM models on games from the clembench suite (Chalamalasetti et al., 2023) and performing two analyses: i) we derive a task-transferability graph using a binary integer optimization program from Zamir et al. (2018), using task performance as the main metric; and ii) we compute task vectors (Ilharco et al., 2022) for each game to study similarities across finetuned models and their task transferability. In our first analysis, we find that some games benefit more from transfer than finetuning, and that the visuospatial family (e.g., exploration games) transfers best. With our task vector analysis instead, we find that similarity-based approaches capture game-role relationships but almost no transferability patterns, suggesting that more complex metrics are required.
